[2025-02-01 21:35] pape_susic : Hi, What does this mean, are we going to lose all 12m from our transfer budget to this upgrade?
[2025-02-01 22:33] faro1 : Hi Pape, nopes, here is how it works:  Every day some money is deducted for Maintenance, as seen in your Daily Flow section of Finances page. This is the only money you actually spend.  You can put more or less than the needed for daily mantainance (100%). This is decided automaticaloy by the board based on your budget and money.  Facilities page is like a separate piggybank (or Facilities Funds) where money from Mantainance comes, and actual mantainance is deducted. Daily change shows how much extra cash was injected. When your reach the Upgrade at: target, your facilities gain half a star. Then the 12M get deducted from that piggybank/funds.

[2025-02-10 11:37] derbymanager : So, when a player starts a dribble or any other action it is tested against the defender. If the defender is better he takes the ball. If the attacker is better - there is a chance the defender will make a foul. The chance for the defender to make a foul depends on prefessionalism and his current condition (tired players make more fouls). There is no skill for the attacker to "stay on his feet" so to say, it only depends on the defender.

[2025-05-12 23:07] poletz : Every monday club reputation is updated. According to your results goes up and down a bit. Promotion give a big boost to it.   So this value affect the money u get (sponsorship deals) but increase also your costs(maintenance)   So the +10k in sponsors is due to better team reputatiob  The +60k from stadium is cause if the upgrade u did  The higher maintence  (-90) is due to: -better facilities (due to the update -better rep (increase the cost) -u r investing now 170% instead than 165% in upgrades (cause u ve better balance and/or more available money)   So basically u r earning +70 and paying -90 . So -20 overall. But u r investing more in upgrades
[2025-05-12 23:07] poletz : Now, the ifa subsidy
[2025-05-12 23:09] poletz : It s just a flat earning same for everybody that is given when there is too few money in the game , so to keep economy stable. But when it happens it s not a good sign ss it means economy overall is not going well

[2025-05-14 14:10] poletz : so i promised to say something about this. basically the game is quite intuitive, u can easily guess that Mar/tac are defensive skills and fin/long shot are instead about offense. there is also an explanation of each skill in the wiki. btw, the game has some tactical depth, so it s not all about their position but also the role u set for them can change a lot their behaviour and so the most important/required skills. u can check each role preference in your team page ("test your tactic" link). here u can see: how much they affect defensive build up and build up (and how much they prevent both) and also how much they like to run with the ball, try long passes, attemps long shots. ecc. all those can change a bit how much a skill matters for them also teams settings and how other players are positioned can affect it a bit. thats why there is not a "best skills for each role" list, cause its  a bit situational. like headers could be important for strikers but if u play avoiding crosses, it became less important.  or fielding the FC as TM or TQ make a big difference. just to make an example..
[2025-05-14 14:10] poletz : also for <@697501461948661770>
[2025-05-14 14:20] poletz : <@1337372452254388255> what did u notice that u feel contacdicting your expections? if u notice something that u think it's weird or unexpected, could be useful if u share it here. so that Derby can give a look into it and considering maybe if a fix is needed. the final aim is to build an intuitive game, where players/teams behave as they would irl

[2025-05-14 18:56] 70fyy_ : The question was more simed on the moment where i look at my DL player and should decide if hes gonna play FB/AWB or WB. On what basis am i deciding that.
[2025-05-14 18:57] 70fyy_ : This is still very helpful tho.
[2025-05-14 19:03] randykeys : for me, i go more by tactical ideology than skills, cus i very often rotate or have someone play their second best position if there are others that are better than them at their first.  FB to me is if i'm playing with say a back four and want more defensive stability and let my midfielders and attackers handle the offense.  WB in that regard is the more offensive role that can work in a back four with an HM to cover, or as i prefer it, in a back five, while also utilising another winger further up.  AWB i mostly use when i have no other wingers in front of them, letting them have free reign, along with a back five to cover when they're up in attack and can't get back in time.  IWB i like having when my midfield is mostly BTB and CM to cover in the middle when the opponent launches a counter, probably best with MLR too to cover the flank, tho i never play MLR so take that with a grain of salt lol.  again this is all just my "feeling", i can't prove if any of this actually works or not, just that right now my "gut" tells me WB works well, along with IWB, FB is a safe option but often doesn't do much, and AWB i feel should be stronger, but it's not worked for me as well as the others, so, can't say much about it.
[2025-05-14 19:04] randykeys : long story short, when in doubt or unsure of what works best, i default to FB

[2025-06-16 15:52] poletz : wiki says: "For defensive build up attackers use Creativity + Positioning vs opponents' Pressing and Agility. For other build ups the engine tests Creativity + Passing vs Pressing + Positioning."  Not sure this is still 100% true as derby changed things a little bit several times, but quite safe to say that CRE is the most important skill for BU and PRE is the most important skill for PreventBU.   so for each player u need to calculate "skills power" x "role contribution. to simplify let s use cre for bu and pre for pbu  bpd has 9 in DefensiveBU contribution. if he has 10 in cre, his DBU contribution is 90 then sum all players total dbu power ( and same for bu , pdbu and pbu) just an example about the mechanic, numbers are not so high as u can see.
[2025-06-16 16:15] poletz : dwg has 7 contribution to prevent side bu, so your bu power is 8 (of the wg, fb doesn t contribute) vs 7 of his dwg  (remember u ve to multiply it for skills, assuming cre and pre are close (i can t waste scouts but it seems like it) the output is fair  on the other direction <- , dwg has 4 bu contribute , against the 5 of your fb (wg doesn t contribute). so also there multiply for skills, he has low cre u ve low pre, so close. final output is close to 50/50 also there and it s fair.  this just to try to explain how it works rn. hope it can help (u actually are doing wonders ignoring this all so doesn t seem to be a key factor eheh)
[2025-06-16 16:17] poletz : rn is much more important to use the right roles/lineup in the part of the match that is actually played than trying to minmax this hidden part of bu generation (probably a good thing)

[2025-07-06 20:22] derbymanager : So, a quick recap of finances, again:  - Stadium revenue and match rewards are not included in daily finances as they're variable of course. You might play a home game and a cup game in one day and earn a lot, and then the next two days you can play away and earn 0. - Instead, the board uses an estimated daily stadium revenue. So, they expect you will earn 1M from today's home game, then 0 from tomorrow's away game, and so on for the whole season. Average is 500k per day and they use that for their calculations. - Based on that they will invest into facilities as much as they can without going too far into negative daily money. They also won't invest into facilities if they estimate your facilities are too high for the league.  So why are my facilities downgrading?  Because you don't have enough money to invest into them. Let's say you just sold a player and have 5M on your account. The board is downgrading your facilities by 200k per day to keep those 5M intact so you can buy players. They could, instead, keep your facilities at 100% and they wouldn't downgrade, but you would lose 200k per day and in less than a season (25 days to be exact) you would lose those 5M and couldn't improve your squad.  Since your facilities downgrade for the same price it costs to improve them you can just buy back the level you lost for cash, assuming you have cash to do so. Financially and mathematically it is exactly the same. There is no benefit if the board is investing money for you or if you do it manually yourself. It's just moving money from one bucket into another.  Hope that helps.  Also, I made a change in the morning that will invest more into facilities but you need to wait for the night update to update your finances. Tomorrow they'll invest a bit more into facilities 🤞

[2025-07-31 09:32] experimental3800 : Hey, I'm new here. Game looks quite promising. [2025-07-31 09:56] derbymanager : The game is changing pretty fast as it's still in beta while I try to balance it all... The best approach is to simply ask here on discord and people will help you out.  From the design perspective, the goal is to reward having a balanced team, a mixture of mentors, youth prospects and everything in between. Whenever there is a perceived meta I try to nerf it so that it isn't the best (or only) way to play. Even if one approach is perhaps too good at the moment, you can count on it getting worse in the future.  In terms of how to play, my suggestion would be: - Analyse your team, make sure you have good players all around for the formation you intend to play (it's enough to just look at the stars in the squad selection screen). Don't shy away from playing players out of position, they'll learn the new position and will play well there in 5-10 games. - Generally speaking, 1 or 2 bad players in your squad won't break you. You can play a formation that you know works well and fill a position or two with 500k youngster if needed. Of course, better players usually mean better results, but that's not guaranteed and prepare that you'll get angry at match engine occasionally 😬 - If you need money you can sell one good player and buy two ok ones. For example, you sell Valle and buy two 5-8M players to fill up your squad with 3.5 star players. You have a lot of youngsters, maybe offload those you don't intend to play and buy another 5-8M player. Selling shitty players might be tough, though. - Your main goal should be to go up to 3rd division. Don't worry about player development, facilities, or anything else. I would buy older (25+) quality players that will push you up. The rewards basically double with each division so you want to get as high as possible as fast as you can.
[2025-07-31 10:02] questionmark4 : How is the offers on job offers decided? Because i have looked around based on reputation there should be better teams there for me
[2025-07-31 10:08] derbymanager : I realized I didn't answer almost any of your questions 😅   > Like what to do at the start - which players do I sell, which players are worth buying at the start? Try to have 15 players with 3-4 stars in your squad. Better to have a good average squad than few top players and the rest all shitty ones. > How does the yout school work, when to promote youths? For a season you can observe 4 players in youth school. After 3 weeks you'll see their potential and all skills. If you like them, you can hire them. If you don't, you can find a new player at any time. When they reach their training limit in the school there will be a message so you can promote them if you think they'll get some playtime in your squad.  > Are players who are reaching their peak at the club worth keeping or should I get rid of them? On the training screen you can see a yellow or red icon that the player is close to reaching their peak in your team. That means that they could still grow but would need a better team to do so. If you're about to get promoted it might be worth keeping them. Otherwise you might consider selling them and buying some that can grow or that won't be unhappy. Having a couple unhappy players is ok, having half of the team unhappy is problematic. There is no right or wrong way, assess your squad and decide. * > What is sharpness and how important is it? Sharpness is increased by playing games and it's pretty important but not so much to avoid playing a good player with low sharpness. It grows quickly and it's basically here to promote rotating your squad so that you'd have more than 11 players ready to play at all times. > How much do mentors really contribute to the training? Quite a lot. They boost your facilities. > If I got w low-division club am I stuck with it for a longer time and should prepare to build it or do I get offers from better teams relatively soon? You'll get offers from better teams when you go up into 3rd division and survive there.

[2025-08-01 00:06] furysk : For tier 4 teams i'd say that a guide would be:  have 3-4 players that are Lower division completed products.  these guys will want to lead a young team more than an established player might.  Ideally, you can also find players that will be prominent in a few different formations.  For example, a strong lower division 23-26 year old that can play a defensive game will usually have a lot of use, as will a more complete central defender.  whereas a veteran fullback winger or wide forward might not get the same amount of utility overall.  Pick and choose a few guys that can grow into the mentor position at the minimum, do not sell mentors unless you have a surplus in that age group.  Be willing to lose their TL potential, you are paying for their benefit to your team by missing on a few million.  Understand what each role does in the formation in this game, some roles do things slightly different than perhaps your favorite manager would use them IRL.  the tactics test screen is a good spot to see what the impact of each role is.  Spend a little bit more on the right unpredictable youngsters that have skills where you want it.  In tier 4, those guys that are ideally 2.5 stars but occasionally 2 stars, have high potential, and have great or superb natural fitness are most ideal.  They may be slightly worse than the 3 stars in terms of counting ratings, but they'll be easier to keep happy on lower facilities/mentors which will offset some of that.  The stars are almost less important to me than the spots where the ratings are best right now, have a good chunk of 2.5 stars that are super happy, and the turnaround since they have taken over for unhappy 3.5 stars is night and day (2-4-8 W-D-L first 14, 11-2-2 last 15), although tactical decisions have helped too.  the added bonus with 2.5's is cheaper wages, which means more cash in bank for you 🙂  others can help more beyond 4 than i can, just throwing what i know for this level 🙂

[2025-08-08 15:36] poletz : Each role has a different contribution to defensive build up, build up, prevent defensive build up and prevent build up.  This number is multiplied for his ability in each of those 4. U can see skills involved in one of the last updates.  So all players contribution in each phase are summed and u ve the value u see in the post match report.  Es: def bu : 49/27 (64%) The math is 49/(49+27) = 64%  It means that 64% of ur def bu attempts will be succesful Hence the other number u ve there : 32/51. Is not exactly 64% cause there are other little modifiers but more or less it s this.  Same for all the others .  If u attack from right to left your numbers are those on the right, and viceversa for the other side.  Numbers of def bu actions attempted are always around 50/60. Some of them are turned to counters according to settings and lineups. So it can became lower, imagine 45. Then of this 45 the succesful can be 30. Then this 30 is splitted among left/center/right bu. Those are ur attempts to bu there and also there same math to se how many are succesfull. These will be your action (and add counters to this)  Hope this can help. Told this u can play ignoring bu, it s not so important 🙂

[2025-08-27 21:22] skuld6666 : Amazing suggestion. We absolutely need this. Just a few quick/answers suggestions that hopefully others can build on for now:  - First of all take a good scan through your team and highlight any low potential/low skill/low fitness youths you can try and sell (think you have a few). Or high wage players that just are not that good or are declining fast. Really bad youths you may have to just release. - A core principle of DM2 is that you do need some experience through your team or it doesn't function well. We are sworn enemies of the classic Football Manager squad of U22 wonderkids here.... - Next look through for any gems who have contracts expiring and at least make a note that when funds allow you can try and sign a new contract. Note: all contracts are 3 years so do weigh up carefully if they are old and they may decline in that time or young and you will want to sell/release/upgrade them pretty soon.... - Next try and piece together your best 11 with 3-4 possible subs in a sensible formation - say 4-5-1, 4-4-2 or 5-4-1 for tough away matches.  - Looks like you have a decent couple of GKs which is really key. However, could even sell one and promote a youth cheaply from your team's school as backup?  - You also seem OK for strikers from a quick glance (I can't see without scouting them), but not great for midfield or defence. First signing might be a central defender? - It's REALLY hard to get sacked. The board will be more strict when the game is stable. - It's a pretty slow game - keep moving the team in the right direction. Getting out bad players and bringing in betters ones. Patience is needed and rewarded. - Scout reports are GOLD. Never waste them! You start with 20. Generate at 3 new ones per day.
[2025-08-27 23:29] furysk : from recent experience as someone in IV who was 7-10-20 in their first 37 and 27-6-6 in the last 39, the things that made it work for me after a while:  1) Do not build to a formation that works for someone else.  they have the players to make it work, you probably dont, so just build your team based on what you have to work with early on.  The only formations that tend not to work as easily (though still doable) are ones that aren't somewhat symmetrical.  It takes some good studying to make them work, best to not go that route until you feel like you have a good understanding.  2) Do not chase guys with high potential unless your plan is to then spin said player.  Happiness once those players hit the maximum for the level will plummet, and you'll have volatile performances.  If you can buy a player for 1-1.5M and get them to grow a lot and sell them for 4.5-5M, then fair play, but the idea of having that guy be the cornerstone of the franchise isn't feasible unless your teams growth is really significant (meaning you are in tier 1 in 4-5 seasons)  3) Look at literally any player that can help you now.  Experience is great, but if you can find the right guy that is 22-25 and is near the end of development, make them your tier 4 cornerstone and hope they accept a backup contract down the road or they can be sold to be someone elses tier 4 winning player.  I only know of your MC/FC, as i listed him this season, you have a solid False Nine and a good attacking-minded midfielder there.  iirc I even made him work at holding mid, though that wasn't the ideal setup.  I can give you some thoughts in <#1102891926371438623> for what you have i guess in brief

[2025-08-29 03:31] furysk : My Opinion, which is not that of an expert nor a high level player but as one who is currently making the effort to guide his team out of tier 4 to what appears to be a decent shot at working:   Sell the strongest 'ceiling' prospects that you have.  it is my strong opinion that in tier 4 and to some extent tier 3 that their happiness is too much to maintain.  Need good mentors, need good facilities, need playing time to keep playing shape up to get the most out of it.  you can offer them the 3rd, but it at some point is no longer enough.  Once you have your team going the right direction, some more high-solid/established-great/superb types (potential, ceiling, fitness) may have a better chance of being brought up alongside your club, especially if you manage to set up for a multi-promotion run which is doable from 4 to 2 but not a guarantee.  I think it's best to see what works on your own as far as the blend of things, but i would say having a good mix of starters that are best suited for fringe tier 3-4 play + some solid youngsters with skills in the right spots + 3-4 mentors is the most ideal setup on the wage budget you'll have to operate on.  Too many veterans and your wages spiral out of control, too many youths and your results get volatile.    You can make it work without selling the guys with some good $$ values on their heads right now, but that road will take a few weeks to hit positive cash flow, maybe more if you can't win some games.

[2026-01-19 23:36] furysk : 1st question -  Build up is based on creativity, dribbling, first touch and tier... Prevent build up on anticipation, positioning, tackling and tier.  Tier has a huge impact on it, in tier 4 i would basically say don't worry about it too much
[2026-01-19 23:39] furysk : 3rd Question  - Action Resolution i believe is covered in the <#1102892256630943754> under Match Engine.  The info is a bit outdated, as you'll see my answer to point 1 is not the same as it was listed there, but i think that will be the closest you get to an answer outside of Derby or maybe one of the mods coming in with more knowledge.
[2026-01-19 23:46] furysk : 2nd question - what is most important from stats/ratings is pretty wide ranging, could get 5 people that answer 5 different ways.  I'll say this much, this game more than any other game is going to reward you for keeping players at least partially happy and deeper into their careers moreso than other games.  The Shape of your player determines their volatility in performance.  Veterans with experience (not to be confused with late spawning 25-30 year olds on non-playable teams) will largely not go into the red form, which is part of the calculation.  If you can keep them Green or Blue for the most part in happiness, then they are likely to be mostly Green, Blue, and occasionally yellow in Shape, which means likely good performance, likely solid performance, and inconsistent performance.  Red is will likely under perform.  From there, i'd say <#1102892256630943754> posts on skills, posts 1 and posts 3 in there are important reads.
[2026-01-19 23:48] furysk : I don’t use any formulas in terms of math, I just give grades to specific attributes, hidden ratings like composure adaptability or professionalism, and individualistic vs team players.

[2026-02-13 00:51] furysk : Stadium impacts 'estimated stadium revenue' in the daily flow portion of your financials page, and will usually make it easier to balance your overall budget to where you lose less maintenance costs.  in tier 3 your stadium is capacity * 10 to see your max stadium revenues.  your 23k stadium should be capable of getting you 230k if it maxes out.  since you are not maxed out, an additional stadium increase doesn't actually do much for you financially short term.  Sponsorship facility will impact sponsorship deals in the Allowed salaries section.  It will increase your wage budget by 75-80k (75k guaranteed, the multiplier might give it an additional 5k for finishing 12th it's a 1.05 multiplier).
[2026-02-13 00:54] furysk : If you increase sponsors, you will hopefully run into one of two scenarios:  you spend 0 of that additional wage capacity, and your Maintanence cost cutting goes from 25% to 0-5%, and you stay were you are.  or  you spend it all, keep your facilities sliding backward short term, however if it means being more competitive you should be able to get the stadium to max capacity, netting you not only the 75k wage increase, but also the 50k difference between your current 178k and the 230k max stadium revenues, which would then keep your facilities just as balanced as before give or take.
[2026-02-13 00:59] furysk : If that is a bit convoluted let me know and i'll try again 😄

[2026-04-02 12:55] derbymanager : should be fixed now
[2026-04-02 13:04] derbymanager : Your personal reputation always slowly moves towards your club's reputation (faster when going up, slower down). In d4 this usually means you need to get to d3 and survive 1 season to get your personal reputation above 200.  Your team's reputation works in the same way - it slowly moves to the reputation it should have if it was in this position. The bigger the difference, the faster it moves (in both cases).  You get a boost to your reputation (for purposes of switching teams) the longer you are with one team and the higher you bring them before switching. So, for example, getting selhurst to d2 would improve your reputation through above mentioned means, but would also give you a boost of IDK 40 points for going from d4 to d2, and another boost of 30 points for staying with the team for 3 seasons or whatever (numbers are not correct).
[2026-04-02 13:05] derbymanager : It's a relative power between the two teams based on the calculated power of each player. Not especially precise but it gives you a bit of an indicator who was the more powerful team of the two.

Your teams reputation on that sort of week even if 1 or 2 opponents were weakish in terms of reputation should've moved up some. I think at your position in the table right this minute, you are looking at a position that should be about 125 reputation, so the difference of 23 points means that 105-107 is within reach. I think it's a team that is capable of playing to the 4th-6th best team, which is closer to 155-165 range team rep wise for balancing, and by seasons end you will be able to invest in the facilities to get probably more wage budget with sponsors.  I think the team you took should take 2-3 seasons overall to turn around.  so your goal should be to:  end of this season - have an average age of 24, have a viable team financially, push closer to 125 team reputation. end of next season - have an average age of 24.5, have a viable team financially, get to 125 before seasons end by finishing around 5th-6th place at worst, and upgrade sponsorship facilities to get more cash flow and budget to your team (requires 125 rep) end of the following season - upgrade with new budget, average age remaining in the 24.5 range, and promote.  this game is not built to suit those players who wish to zero to hero in 3-4 seasons.  IMO it's more a 6-10 season journey pending the starting point of the team you take.  your ability to take tier 2 or tier 3 sides will come a season after you promote.

[2026-04-07 21:11] furysk : As was noted, you have 15 -> 10 as your facilities.  15 is your current level, 10 is where they recommend a 100-124 reputation should be at facilities wise.  Once you win enough games to get to 125 reputation, you will hit 15 -> 11, and there will be a button that shows up.  Your reputation is 186 as a manager, under ~202-203 reputation you get tier 4 offers, and you get tier 3 offers as your highest offer once you get into the low to mid 200's.  You might get offers from clubs above your reputation, but they wont be hundreds above your reputation.
[2026-04-07 21:22] furysk : If you wanted my personal opinion on what i would do if i had Selhurst, i would probably ship out the highest wage with the lowest 'value'.  in this case, Benitez would go if it were me. If Red is zero and Green is 10M, then the inexperienced plays at 5M over the course of the season, and the veteran probably plays at 8-8.5M, the difference in contributions or games where you can use the veteran are far higher, so you gain more out of them. However, doing the math with a 0-10m is much easier to communicate, so i cut corners 😄  I'd be looking at veterans at tier 4 in 3 ways  1) If they are experienced, they will play better 2) If they are experienced, they will improve happiness from players looking for a mentor 3) If they are mentors, then they eventually will retire and return between 1M and 3M to the facilities, taking the impact of their salaries out of the equation.  You should aim to have an experienced player at every rank of the formation in tier 4 is my personal opinion.  If you can afford another one or two go for it.

[2026-08-14 18:46] derbymanager : Think of facilities as a bet in the context of youths.   Obviously, training is one of the best ways to earn money in the main squad. Buy a player, train him, sell for more.  With youngsters the price is basically 0, or close to it, even if players are worth several million. So:  - small facilities: you can get just about anyone, train them, promote them, train them more, sell them for small profit. - big facilities: you need great youngsters, train them, promote them, train them more, sell them for big profit.  So, facilities help you train them but also lock you out of shitty youngsters. You need to find those 3M+ on the market, get them to 7M to turn profit. With low facilities (which should be in low divisions) you can take a 1M player, get him to 3M and still earn money.   Facilities just increase the stakes you are playing with. In a casino you would be at the black jack table with $1000 chips, while d4 team would drop coins into a slot machine 🙂
[2026-08-14 18:48] derbymanager : As for their salary demands, think of it as some sort of unionised contract or something. You get into the school and the reward for those who make it is this contract. All players compete for the same reward. It's up to you to decide who earned it and who didn't.
[2026-08-14 18:50] derbymanager : Finally, it's really not that high. If you take into account the fact that the player joins for free - you can't get a better deal on the market. The only way you can fuck this up is to hire a completely atrocious < 1M player...

[2026-08-15 14:55] derbymanager : So, to give a bit of an overview:  When you promote a player their price is lower because they haven't played any games so there is no performance multiplier on price yet. So the price you see when you promote someone from school is lower than what that player is actually worth. But if you use that price and find the player with the same price and age on the market, just compare the costs. Include the cost of school, contracts, everything until the end of their first professional contract.  For someone with facilities in the 40s total cost for 1 school year + 3 first team years is about 6M. For someone with facilities in the 20s total cost is about 3M.  A 2M player will cost you about 5M to get from the market (with 3 years of salaries and the signing fee).  Financially, even if you miss and promote a bad player, you basically can't miss with youngsters. You would have to promote <1M players that can't grow in your squad and can't be sold to actually lose money... The fact is that the youngsters were and, especially now, are too good investment.   Which brings me to the real problem and that is the money drain from the game. Every youngster that gets promoted is money that goes out of the game. Keeping them in school drains the money from the game. Buying them from the free market into the school drains the money from the game. It affects the market negatively. D4 teams don't have to trade among themselves, they can get their entry-level players from schools instead. Why would you buy 2M player when you can get him for 0?  I like the system, I like scouting youngsters, but it's problematic (and not because you can't promote all of them). So expect even more updates with restrictions and discouragement from using them 😬

[2026-10-05 11:22] stock_93_29331 : If you’re pressing with a low defensive line how does that work or what does that look like? Pressing says press all over the pitch! So when does the defensive line step up if you are playing with a low line? It sounds like a bit of an oxymoron
[2026-10-05 11:31] derbymanager : normally your players won't try to move too far away from their position to close down opponents in their own pitch (but will do so in your own half). With pressing they will move further away to try to press in both halves, and their range when they'll move in to press increases.  Imagine players A and B are this far apart:   A . . . B1 . . . B2 . . . B3  A would normally move to press B when B is in A's half of the pitch at distance B1 or B2. He would stick to his position and not press B if B is at B3. In the B's half of the pitch A would press only if the player is near on B1 (basically running next to him).  If pressing is turned on, then A will move all the way to B3 to close down the opponent without the ball and will do it in both halves of the pitch, not only in A's half.
[2026-10-05 11:34] derbymanager : Defensive line just positions players on the pitch, they follow the pressing explained above relative to their position. So low block, players are positioned deeper, and press in their relative area deeper on the pitch.
[2026-10-05 11:42] stock_93_29331 : So does that mean with a low defensive line they cover more distance to press

And then there are players supporters slowly build their football lives around without even noticing.  Andrzej Wieland was the second kind. Just fourteen seasons of reliability. Millwall were lumping crosses into the box nonstop. And Andy just shrugged at me like, ‘This is fine.’”  Ackermann paused before continuing.  “That’s what he gave the club for fourteen years. Basically, it’s time to shape the player into a first-team starter!  From now on, it’s time to consider their current abilities and the amount of match minutes you are able to provide them

[2024-06-13 10:03] derbymanager : So, I just checked, a player will fully learn a new role/position (it doesn't matter which) in 6-20 games assuming he gets average on random every time. In theory he could get 0 on random for all eternity and never learn, but that's highly unlikely. Whatever penalty he gets is halved in about 2-4 games already so the risk isn't that big.   Note that each role has its own knowledge level so a MC BTB might have MC HM at 0 and get the full penalty from the role. On top of that is if he isn't a MC at all.  The only limitation is that gk and outfield players can't learn each other's positions at all.  Training is reduced by how well he knows the role and only about half of it (e.g. with 0 knowledge he will still train). So teaching players a new role once or twice in their career won't stagger their development. But doing it constantly might have a significant effect.  Players also forget roles they didn't play in. The better knowledge for the role, the slower it gets forgotten. e.g. a role that's at 0.5 knowledge might disappear in a few games, but from 1.0 to 0.5 might take a whole season.

[2024-08-02 08:25] derbymanager : This is exactly what we have now 🤔   I feel the oldies-benefit is not tangible, and it's not nearly as good as young player's. In d4 you get 2M for winning the league, 4M in d3. Everything below that is proportionally lower.  So if you can buy a 2M player and you have two options: A.) 31yo that has skills at 12 B.) 21yo that has skills at 10  Let's say that with player A you'll finish 1st and with B you'll finish 4th. In reality I doubt 1 player can make such difference but let's assume the most extreme scenario. That's a difference of maybe 500k in d4, 1M in d3... Probably lower because the difference in money between 1st and 4th is bigger than between 11th and 14th.  Player A will lose some value in that season, so whatever you earn extra will be lower. Keep in mind that we already assumed huge impact of this single player on your final position. It's not unbelievable that any extra you earn is completely negated with this one old player.  There is also boost to your reputation and possibly higher earnings later on if you get promoted, but that only matters if with that old guy you get promotion and without him you don't, which probably isn't the case for most teams.  There's also passive training boost, but that makes that player lose even more value...  On the other hand if you go with player B, there is a chance that player will earn you those 500k or 1M simply from training. Even if he stagnates, he most likely won't lose value.  In addition, player B will be better next season while player A will be worse. If in first season player B got you +3 positions on the league table, in 2nd season it'll be +1 position, and third season  B player is better.  ---  Now do the same math with 5 players and the gap becomes bigger and bigger.

And B could have xG of 1 against him and suffer from 0 to 2 goals. And sure, when A concedes 0 he will get a better rating than B that conceded 0, but when A concedes 4 he will get a worse rating than B when he concedes 2. On average, they will (should) concede the number of goals equal to xG and xG itself won't make much difference.
[2024-08-10 20:53] poletz : In theory yes. But we ve fringe gks getting 9.5 rating just cause the rng made 3+ xg being 0 goals. While the clean sheet has nothing to do with his ability. [2024-08-10 20:58] derbymanager : Ratings are not precise and that's ok. You have a bigger problem with distribution for all positions. The player did the same, but got better rating in one case. I've never seen anyone get below 3 rating except for goalkeepers so they're on the other end - one catastrophic game can ruin their average... [2024-08-27 10:37] derbymanager : This is really a good example. The first shot probably had high xg. It depends which calculation you use, some also take into account defender's positioning, but the shot was basically without pressure and from within the box. Gk saved it. The second shot had something like 0.8 but it wasn't Gk's fault, defenders didn't run back and cover the runner. But nevertheless, the only one who prevented this action was the gk, even if he was lucky for the attacker to miss in the end. If it were a goal, gk's rating would be 6, this way it is 6.5...  In real life the striker would be rated 5.5 instead of 6 based on this one miss. It depends on the rest of the game ofc, but surely his rating would drop... But the DM match engine will give the striker that missed the empty goal higher rating simply for taking a shot. And his xG will be huge, making his average xg per shot higher. You'll see him as a good striker but at the same time the gk shouldn't get the benefit of using match stats to his advantage?

[2024-08-27 10:52] derbymanager : Anyway, there are several cases in DM: 1.) two equally good teams, eg. salty vs poletz 2.) one team much better than the other, e.g. cup game 3.) two equally good teams but one is fielding dc as fc or gk and has trouble bringing out the correct team  with current xg: 1.) you know who did tactically better, and I think that's the most important thing anyone wants to know. 2.) your xg is higher than it should be because the other team is weaker. Does it matter if you won 3:0 with 3xg or 1.5xg? In real life it would show 1.5xg and it would look like you overperformed xg. Since you only see 1.5xg and you don't know that the "real" xg was 3 you can only guess the impact the difference in power had. 3.) you have to check why you had high xg and probably, since you know you fielded your best team, the reason is the gk or defenders.  with real world xg: 1.) player abilities don't matter so you don't know who did tactically better, we can only guess 2.) xg is 1.5 but you scored 3. how much was gk responsible for that? who knows 3.) the two teams might have similar xg, so you can't tell how much of an impact the wrong players had and how much it was luck  Basically, for adjusted xg you have two variables, ability and luck that you have to guess and there is no way to know exactly how much of an impact they had. With current xg you have only one variable, ability, and you can calculate luck.

[2024-09-03 08:25] poletz : - Implemented momentum (or psychology or whatever you want to call it) that will increase losing team's build up power and decrease it for the winning team if the winning team has an early lead or leads by a lot. So, if your team is winning by a lot they will attack less while the opponent will attack more. Same goes if they score an early goal or two, they will naturally slow down a bit and the other team will take initiative. - How good your players are at getting back from behind depends on work rate and experience. How much will they slow down when they are in the lead depends on focus and experience (the lower their focus, the more they slow down). Note that only build up is affected, preventing build up is not affected by this. Note also that this kicks in exponentially so it barely makes any difference in close games. The intention is to give a bit of breathing room to a seriously weaker opponent. Basically, to make 5:0 results look like 3:1 perhaps, it won't make a difference between two equal teams playing 1:0 but it might help we get some surprise results.

[2024-09-13 07:51] derbymanager : Attack trhough wings is not a huge issue. The way it works is that it rates passes towards the sides better (so that the passer would pick them more often). If there's nobody there, well, central passes will look the best. So when the animation starts it basically has no effect. It does have effect on abstracted build up step where it'll test side build up more often. If side build up succeeds, the ball will be generated on the side and closest player (e.g. DL or MLC) will be put next to the ball to start an action. Messina had around 85% success rate on side build up while Cittadella had about 50%, and almost half of their build ups went there so it was suboptimal in that way... But after the action is prepared/generated it didn't do much on resolution...
